header:
import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open Set MeasureTheory
namespace BasisObjects
abbrev Rn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
noncomputable def content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
      ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
def euclideanLift (n : ℕ) : Rn n × ℝ → WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2
end BasisObjects

namespace IntervalProduct
abbrev Rn := BasisObjects.Rn
def I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def F (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn n × ℝ) := E ×ˢ I
def j (n : ℕ) (p : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ)) : Rn (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => p.fst i) p.snd)
def unj (n : ℕ) (v : Rn (n + 1)) : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => v i.castSucc), v (Fin.last n))
def G (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn (n + 1)) :=
  j n '' (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' F n E)
noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
  letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
  MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A
noncomputable def cost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a
noncomputable def realCost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam (U i))) ^ a
def Cover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
def RealCover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ (∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (U i)) ∧ ∀ i, Metric.diam (U i) ≤ δ
end IntervalProduct
open IntervalProduct
representation: n is the original natural n₀, including zero; E remains a subset of BasisObjects.Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Ordinary X × ℝ uses Mathlib's maximum product metric. WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) uses the L² product metric: here 2 is the extended nonnegative real exponent, not the coordinate count. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 over Fin n. The explicit j appends the last real coordinate with Fin.snoc and unj truncates at castSucc and reads Fin.last; T009 proves this is a bijective isometry. G is exactly the set of coordinate concatenations of E and I, as an image under these explicit functions, in Euclidean Rn(n+1). E001 transports dimension from the maximum product to the L² product; no unproved metric identification is definitional. H fixes the canonical Borel measurable structure locally, avoiding any extra measurability premise on X or A. content is the exact frozen basis definition; powers are ENNReal real powers, infima/suprema and nonnegative sums remain in ℝ≥0∞ with ∞ allowed. cost retains the nonempty-member supremum; for positive exponents an empty member costs zero. RealCover explicitly includes boundedness before using real diameters, and realCost uses their nonnegative finite casts. Cover is the finite extended-diameter condition, equivalent to RealCover at positive real scales. N004 supplies finiteness before any use of NNReal representatives or toReal; standard cast order/addition compatibility does not add an assumption. No M premise ports or background-note premise ports are introduced. The pinned product metric instances require Fact (1 ≤ p): this is a proof that the Lp exponent lies in the metric range, and at p=2 it is supplied by the library, not an additional project hypothesis. The pinned Prod.dist_eq is max of the coordinate distances. Fin n indexes exactly the initial n coordinates; Fin.castSucc preserves their values in Fin(n+1), and Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. In cost and content, ^ a has real exponent a on ENNReal; in the squared-distance formulas ^ 2 is the ordinary natural square of a real distance.

      BasisObjects.content (s + 1) (ENNReal.ofReal δ) (A ×ˢ I)) ∧
  H s A ≤ H (s + 1) (A ×ˢ I)

explanation: Export N006 on the original domain. For the finite real representatives d,k, handle d=0 using the fibre bound k≥1. If d>0 and k<d+1, use the source midpoint s=(k-1+d)/2; it is positive, less than d, and s+1>k. The critical-exponent infinite-measure theorem, N003 and the dimension lower bound from infinite measure contradict this. Antisymmetry with N005 gives equality. N004 gives finiteness and includes n=0. H002 remains an original project premise although this source argument does not use compactness.

source_steps.text: By N004 write D,T as casts of real values d_real≥0 and k_real≥1. Their orders and addition agree with real operations. If L3: d_real=0, the fibre bound k_real≥1 gives k_real≥d_real+1. Discharge L3 to retain this implication. Since d_real≥0, the other case is d_real>0.

Assume L1: d_real>0. To prove the lower bound, assume for contradiction L2: k_real<d_real+1. Then 0≤k_real-1<d_real by F001. Put s_mid=(k_real-1+d_real)/2. These inequalities imply 0<s_mid<d_real and k_real<s_mid+1. The strict positivity of s_mid follows from d_real>0 even if k_real-1=0.

By F002, M002 applied to E at the nonnegative exponent s_mid gives H^s_mid(E)=∞, because dimH(E)=D is the cast of d_real. N003, applied with X=Rn(n₀), A=E and s=s_mid, gives H^s_mid(E)≤H^(s_mid+1)(F). Consequently H^(s_mid+1)(F)=∞.

M005 with A=F and the nonnegative exponent s_mid+1 yields s_mid+1≤T from F003, equivalently s_mid+1≤k_real by F001. This contradicts F002. Discharge L2 and conclude k_real≥d_real+1 under L1. Discharge L1, and combine with the d_real=0 implication in F001 by exhaustive cases on d_real≥0. Hence k_real≥d_real+1 for all cases.

F004 gives T≥D+1, and N005 gives T≤D+1. Antisymmetry proves T=D+1. Both dimensions and their sum are finite by F001 and N004. When n₀=0, N004 forces D=0 and the fibre branch already supplies the lower bound; the upper proof also covered this case. This proves the output proposition. Compactness remains an original hypothesis in the global specification, although this replacement proof does not use it.

boundary: Only listed inputs are project premises. The pinned Mathlib environment is freely available; no sibling proof is supplied.

R006.BG001.fact: A metric space, viewed as an emetric space by casting its distance, can be equipped with its Borel measurable structure without any condition on a specified subset. In particular this applies to Rn(n₀) and to MaxProd(Rn(n₀)); their subsets E and F need not be measurable to evaluate the supplied Hausdorff measures on them.

grounds.reason: Rn(n₀) is the specified Euclidean metric space, including n₀=0.
MaxProd has the specified maximum product metric.
H is evaluated using the ambient Borel structure on arbitrary subsets.

R006.BG001.justification: Every metric defines a topology and hence the sigma-algebra generated by its open sets; choosing that sigma-algebra is precisely choosing its Borel measurable structure. The maximum of the two coordinate distances is a metric: separation and symmetry hold coordinatewise, and max(a+c,b+d)≤max(a,b)+max(c,d) proves its triangle inequality from the coordinate triangle inequalities. Casting a finite metric distance gives the compatible emetric structure. These are ambient structure choices; no subset measurability or original hypothesis is added.

R006.BG002.fact: For u,v∈ℝ≥0∞, if u=∞ and u≤v then v=∞.

grounds.reason: N003 compares H^s(E) to H^(s+1)(E×I) in ℝ≥0∞ for every positive s.
M002 gives infinite H^s(E) when the nonnegative exponent is below dimH(E).
F001 identifies dimH(E) with the cast of d_real.
F002 establishes 0<s_mid<d_real, enabling both cited inputs.

R006.BG002.justification: Substitution gives ∞≤v. Since ∞ is the top element, also v≤∞; antisymmetry gives v=∞.
